# Registered effect layers and ordered completion

This local implementation replaces per-field effect ownership with one world
engine. It is one prerequisite of the complete field display query, not that
query itself. Read [the field inventory](live-field-display-ownership-audit.md)
for the actual field descendants and excluded World siblings.

## Source phases

Original paths are relative to the sibling research repository's `re/bt3`:

- `export_scripts/scripts/_-0D.as:976–990`: a queue holds the already constructed
  clip, supplied coordinates, layer name, rotation flag and callback. It does not
  attach that clip. `_‑2c.CreateEffect` resolves the first registered matching
  name, applies the caller's writes, adds the same clip and appends a completion
  record (`export_pcode/scripts/_-2c.pcode:237–339`).
- `_-2c._-8o`, `_-Z7` and `_-0S` append registrations, resolve the first name and
  unregister the first name, respectively. Removing a name is not removeChild.
  The old physical parent and the currently resolved name can therefore differ.
- `_-2c.Run` first collects every ready clip identity. `_‑9p` invokes its callback
  while attached, rereads the indexed completion record, removes through current
  layer-name resolution and then splices the record. A callback-created record
  is retained but is absent from the preceding ready snapshot. Callback failure
  prevents the following removal. See AS `_-2c.as:262–304,343–362` and qualified
  pcode's `_‑9p` callback-before-remove chain around1664–1676.
- `BTAGameWorld._-4j` clears the registered engine without callbacks, unregisters
  outgoing top/bottom, deactivates and detaches the old layers, then promotes and
  registers the next ones (`BTAGameWorld.as:312–392`). The screen layer persists.
  Next-field queues still resolve outgoing registrations before that promotion.

## Implementation and authoritative reads

`RegisteredEffects` separates concrete top/bottom/screen layer instances, ordered
name registrations, actual ordered children and ordered completion records.
`parent(clip)` and `owned(layer)` read physical ownership. A bottom layer belongs
to its actual field's nested lower container; top/screen are World siblings.
Creating a next wrapper constructs its layer identities without registering them.
Reads do not create layers, move clips, draw random values or advance clocks.

`FieldRuntime.effects` is a read-only compatibility snapshot of the engine's
records. `.pending` includes logical queued carriers as well as registered
carriers; `.queuedCarriers` isolates the former and `effectEngine.pendingFor`
isolates the latter. Their context field supports existing host observations; it is
not a physical parent or the source of the complete geometry population. Do not
build a field query by filtering those snapshots. The query must visit the actual
bottom layer's `owned` children under the wrapper's retained transforms.

World polls one engine instead of filtering separate field arrays. It advances
registered host artwork once, keeps direct controller removal separate, and
clears old records before arrival's Deactivate/cache writes. Queue contents are
not display children and a global engine clear no longer silently overwrites
unprocessed queues in other wrappers. Artificial incoming-effect fixtures now
queue requests explicitly. Artificial gallery replacement explicitly detaches
and reattaches its retained clip objects instead of assigning a runtime array.

The source reread after a callback is intentional: saving an entry or filtering
into a replacement array can erase a newly created callback carrier. A changed
name resolution also cannot silently detach a child from a different parent.
The known layer/record-read/removal errors end the current World listener while
its independent artwork tail continues.

An isolated comparison against preceding commit `b2aa47b` demonstrates two actual
before/after contradictions using the same World operations:

| Observation inside/after a Massive callback              | Before     | After      |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| Newly scheduled carrier survives the callback pass       | 0 retained | 1 retained |
| Earlier callback sees later ready artwork still attached | false      | true       |

Eight new regressions cover those cases plus physical outgoing ownership of
next-field requests, preservation of modified clip identity, duplicate name
registration/first-name removal, callback-before-detach, snapshot completion,
no-callback clearing and arrival promotion. Existing assertions remain; the
previous artificial next-layer callback fixture now uses the one actual outgoing
registered engine and additionally proves next's pending population is empty.

# Ordered actor display ownership

This local follow-up separates the enemy layer's actual children from its enemy
and ally Run arrays. It implements the actor portion of
[the complete field inventory](live-field-display-ownership-audit.md), without
claiming that the complete field query is implemented. The renderer follow-up
below now consumes this actor owner; other field populations remain separate.

## Source contract

`_-0D.SpawnNewEnemy` constructs through `TankData._-Tr`, assigns X/Y, adds the
clip to `enemyLayer_mc`, sets its callback, enables Run and appends the enemy
array. `SpawnNewAlly` follows the same phases after overriding imported life to15.
See the original `export_scripts/scripts/_-0D.as:474–487,1382–1398` and qualified
`export_pcode/scripts/_-0D.pcode:5904–5992` for the ally branch. The bytecode's
jump chain follows X → Y → addChild → SetCallback → intState → array push.

Swarm and mine secondaries (`_-ct/_-Va.as:31–49` and `_-ct/_-AW.as:47–68`) count
summons on `currentBFTarget`, transform their emitter Point into that wrapper,
then call its `SpawnNewAlly`. Both recovered blueprints already have life15.
The host now attaches those births immediately, rather than waiting for their
first actor Run or a later synchronization pass. Its existing emitter adapter
remains; this change does not qualify arbitrary mounted matrices.

The cached `_‑G0` reparenting and raw Run arrays are separate operations. Replacing
an array does not perform `removeChild`. Removing an outer wrapper also leaves
its children parented to the detached layer. A repeated `addChild` moves a child
to the end of the same parent's order. Source arrival, collapse and cached-field
references are indexed in the field inventory and [crossing contracts](crossing-source-reference.md).

## Implementation boundary

- `ActorParents.attach/detach` alone mutate ordered membership. `owned(field)`
  reads the actual child order without exposing a mutable Set. A same-parent
  attachment raises the child; a cross-parent attachment removes it from the old
  owner. `sync(world)` updates active ancestry, retained translations, rooted
  state and avatar identity only. It never reads either actor Run array.
- `World.attachActor` combines the source addChild and callback binding, leaving
  array insertion explicit. Fresh/cached field attachment and `spawnEnemy` use
  it. `spawnAlly` constructs at the origin, writes its pose, attaches/binds, then
  appends to the current wrapper's live ally array. Weapon cap checks use that
  same wrapper; the existing emitter Point crosses field coordinate boundaries
  before birth.
- `World.tickActor` no longer repairs parentage or callbacks implicitly. Stage
  artwork enumerates each attached wrapper's owned children, including a child
  absent from both Run arrays. Detached wrappers keep ownership but their clips
  do not advance as stage children. Actual queued removals retain their existing
  source phases; array replacement by collapse/arrival cannot erase a parent.
- Raw host fixtures explicitly import their omitted addChild/SetCallback phase
  through `tools/fixtures/actor-attachments.ts`. This helper is used only by
  artificial unit/browser fixtures. It bootstraps each fixture object once and
  never infers later removal or reparenting. Tests for actual removal now call
  `detach`, and tests for retained raw-array absence preserve attachment. There
  is no production array-discovery fallback. Gameplay births remain explicit.

## Validation and limits

The parent compared the preceding committed implementation (`e76507b`) with this
working implementation using the same literal actor operations. Before/after:

| Operation                                           | Before         | After               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------- |
| Attach enemy2, ally3, enemy4, then synchronize      | 2,4,3          | 2,3,4               |
| Re-add enemy2 to that same parent, then synchronize | 2,4,3          | 3,4,2               |
| Replace both raw arrays with empty arrays           | Child detached | Child retained      |
| One paused stage frame for a display-only child     | Art age0       | Art age1            |
| Swarm/mine birth before first actor Run             | No parent      | Actual field parent |

# Physical field population projection

`simulation/field-population.ts` combines the existing field, actor, pickup and
effect owners into one transient tree. It is local above PR154, whose published
head is unchanged. No application caller uses this seam yet: it is the population
input for the forthcoming separate shape-hit and Script-width traversals, not a
replacement for either query or proof of complete field geometry.

## Source and representation

Read the [complete source inventory](live-field-display-ownership-audit.md),
[field wrapper poses](field-wrapper-state.md), [actor ownership](actor-display-ownership-reference.md),
[pickup ownership](pickup-display-ownership-reference.md) and
[effect registrations](registered-effects-reference.md). Those records retain
qualified source locations and their actual implementation/observation limits.

`readFieldPopulation(world, field)` starts with the actual retained1551 tree.
It retains authored helpers even at zero alpha, both depth-mask nodes/ranges,
all four invisible detail markers and the tutorial's actual parent/frame. The
first tutorial is a root child; later tutorials precede dynamic actors inside
enemyLayer. Numeric inspection of original1667 finds only one nested sprite1658,
with a single frame; the remaining selected-frame children are static text or
leaves. Original bfStartDisplay registers stop scripts on frames1–6. Its chosen
frame is a retained owner read, never inferred from the field's mutable map data.

The projection inserts physical children at their source slots:

| Slot | Authority | Preserved state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| enemyLayer1547 | `ActorParents.owned(field)` | Actual addChild order, Tank object identity, current transform scalars and direct-child tokens |
| lifeBubbleLayer1545 | `PickupDisplays.owned/read` | Actual pickup object, constructor denomination/symbol and existing retained SwfClip |
| bottom117 inside1540 | `RegisteredEffects.owned(actualLayer)` | Physical effect/carrier identity and position, independent of request or completion context |

Top effects, bullets, highlights, screen effects and the avatar are World siblings
and are not inserted into the receiver. Requests do not become display children
until their source queue tail registers them. A destination request can therefore
appear under the outgoing bottom117. A subsequent reparent appears under its
new physical owner even when its compatibility completion context stays old.

No `dead`, alpha, Run-array or UID filter decides membership. WipeTank leaves an
empty owned actor node until actual detach; identical UIDs retain distinct objects.
A detached field still has its actors/pickups, while actual removal of its117
container removes that container from this receiver traversal. It does not erase
the retained engine object's independent parent reference.

Projection nodes and new arrays are frozen. Referenced Tank/Effect/Pickup objects
and qualified pickup trees remain their existing owners' live identities; this
is not a deep historical snapshot. Use the tree synchronously, reread after any
callback or display mutation, and do not cache it using FieldDisplays.revision
alone. Reads perform no attachment/discovery, native construction, stage advance,
entropy draw or UID allocation. Unresolved under-avatar sizing rejects the read.

## Verification

Seven cases exercise the source boundaries above, including next-field queue
ownership and actual layer reparenting, rather than only echoing node counts.
The standalone cases pass49 assertions. Eight isolated import-time mutations
are independently rejected by assertion failures: actor Run-array discovery,
dead filtering, pickup Run-array discovery, admission of queued effects, omitted
masks, omitted detached children, wrong tutorial frame and bypassed size guard.
An unmodified import-time control passes. Production files are never swapped
for these controls.

`bun run format` and `bun run check` pass1,147 tests /17,417 assertions. Exact
logs, mutation preloader/results and the original tutorial's numeric inventory
are retained under ignored `test-results/field-composition/`. Application E2E is
not repeated because this new module has no application caller and changes no
browser flow. The preceding registration correction's twelve passing browser
cases retain their own build/source identity; they are not this seam's E2E proof.

## Remaining integration

This tree covers the modeled physical owners; it is not a geometry provider.
Actor nested artwork/protection, original leaf/text geometry, morphs, drawn
rocket lines, retained generic effect poses, mask conjunctions and per-leaf
Script arithmetic must be supplied before migrating field queries. Dynamic
transform scalars are not advertised as independently qualified full matrices.
Conditional debug helpers and source effect classes outside the modeled offline
roster still require explicit reachability/population handling if introduced.
Do not silently omit an unsupported node, use painted alpha as geometry or treat
a circle/background-only fallback as the complete receiver. Generic-effect clock
qualification remains separate. Global constructor/event/RNG, ordinary earned
progression, Adobe/pixel/audio and complete-game parity remain unproved.

There is no PR, push, merge, deployment or protected-ref change in this local step.

# Damage-beam wrapper query: local design audit

This local follow-up starts at `1ca0d1d91ac8bc4614e1565d62a3f50a5c9790e5`.
It extends the [original wrapper controls](beam-wrapper-geometry-reference.md),
without changing production geometry or claiming to repair the remaining beam
mismatch. PR144 and its combined gate remain the parent's work. There is no
sixth PR, push, merge, deployment, dependency installation or provider change.

The defensible design is a query over a retained field display tree, with
separate geometric-hit and Script-bounds traversal. Current helpers are useful
building blocks, but do not yet supply that complete tree or its exact bounds
arithmetic. Attaching only a background contour and actor hit callbacks would
leave fundamental display-population and transform coverage missing. No partial
replacement is integrated here.

## Source scope and authored geometry

Source paths below are relative to
`/home/ian/Projects/ianwijma/documented-bubble-tank-3/re/bt3`.
Matching qualified pcode remains authoritative over decompiler ordering.

- `_‑14/_‑CO.pcode` retains the per-loop `_‑W.width` read at `ofs03cc` and
  line/mask/cap writes before `_‑W.hitTestPoint(..., true)`. The bullet's parent
  is the world-owned sibling layer; `_‑W` is the field receiver. Neither raw
  damage candidates nor the bullet's own hit result define field membership.
- `BTAGameWorld.as:400–420` / `BTAGameWorld.pcode:1462–1584` place the first
  authored field, attach tutorial artwork, call Setup, rotate `_‑SQ` to180 and
  construct the sibling bullet/effect layers. This probe still does not execute
  that complete Setup or the tutorial's frame scripts.
- New-field setup at `BTAGameWorld.as:1812–1815`, qualified pcode `ofs0591`
  (`8433–8477`), assigns **scaleY then scaleX to four children**:
  `effect_mask_under`, `_‑SQ`, `BF_over_detail_mc`, `BF_BG_mc`. It overwrites the
  authored `_‑SQ` scale; it does not uniformly scale the field root or enemy
  layer. The following source reads `currentBFTarget.width` and the new wrapper's
  width when calculating separation. No transit-spacing production change is
  made here.
- Collapse is a different transform: `_‑0D.as:181–199` changes root scale and
  the separate sibling layers/avatar together. Root-only controls below do not
  reproduce that complete lifecycle.

Re-extraction with existing `decompressSWF` / `extractSymbols(...,{svg:false})`
and `buildDisplayList` confirms symbol1551's relevant frame1 topology:

| Depth | Named child / symbol         | Mask range           |
| ----- | ---------------------------- | -------------------- |
| 1     | `BF_BG_mc` /1537             | none                 |
| 4     | `effect_mask_under` /1539    | through depth8       |
| 6     | `effectLayer_under_mc` /1540 | inside depth4 mask   |
| 10    | `_‑SQ` /1542                 | through depth14      |
| 12    | `avatarUnderBubble_mc` /1544 | inside depth10 mask  |
| 16    | `lifeBubbleLayer_mc` /1545   | outside those ranges |
| 18    | `enemyLayer_mc` /1547        | outside those ranges |
| 20    | `BF_over_detail_mc` /1550    | outside those ranges |

Background shape1536 declares ±8505twips, including a60twip stroke. Exterior
mask shape1541 declares ±13919twips. The mask's authored placement has scale
`0.9924774169921875`, translation(-1,-1)twips. Its raw1391.9px diameter is
therefore not the first field's observed1381.4px width. The existing
`tools/import-swf-geometry.ts` writes the **raw leaf diameter** into
`field-geometry.json`; that value must not be reused as a first-field Script
